inputs.original_text: The IOC is presenting its ban on transgender women and DSD athletes from the female category at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics and future Games as a matter of “fairness and safety.” That sounds less like a neutral safeguard and more like a convenient justification for tightening control over who gets to compete—and for making a political decision look inevitable. When Kirsty Coventry says, “It would not be fair for biological males to compete in the female category,” the certainty of the wording does the work: it closes down debate while the institution gets to define the terms. Don’t assume the official explanation tells you whose interests this decision really serves.
inputs.modified_text: The IOC is dressing a political decision up as “fairness and safety” so it can present exclusion as settled fact. Kirsty Coventry’s line, “It would not be fair for biological males to compete in the female category,” shuts down debate by making the institution’s chosen framing sound unquestionable. This looks less like a neutral safeguard than a coordinated effort to control who qualifies and make that control seem inevitable. The real question is whose interests the IOC is serving—and why it wants us to stop asking.
